title: On the Drowning at the Ford
author: Hlaalu-Teeth, who was not there
unreliability: The author was born forty years after the events he describes and has an interest in them.
text: They came down from the Salt Hills in the dry month, which they thought was clever, and they crossed at the ford, which was not. My great-grandmother opened the fish-weirs upriver. That is all she did. The marsh did the rest, as it does, and afterwards the Dunmer said we had drowned them by sorcery, because it is easier to be beaten by a wizard than by a woman who understood water.
taxon_note: 72 words on a stone; an inscription
